items.title: Sony WH-1000XM4C revives the beloved XM4 with revised hardware
items.summary: SoundGuys argues Sony's WH-1000XM4C - a refreshed take on the fan-favorite XM4 rather than a brand-new flagship - proves the industry does not need a new headphone model every year. Benchmarks show the revamped hardware retains the XM4's class-leading comfort and noise canceling while fixing earlier firmware complaints.

items.title: Oppo Enco X4 TWS earbuds confirmed for September 22 global launch with AI translation and Dynaudio tuning
items.summary: Oppo's Enco X4 flagship earbuds debut globally on September 22 with AI-powered real-time translation, a coaxial dual-driver system co-developed with Dynaudio, a dual DAC, 4K-class lossless transmission (up to 400 percent faster) and a 6nm AI noise-cancellation chip.

items.title: Bose expands audio lineup with colorful open-ear earbuds for audiophiles and runners
items.summary: Bose announced two new wearables: the flagship Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) at 299 dollars and the workout-focused Bose Sport Open Earbuds at 199 dollars. The open-ear design targets audiophiles who want ambient awareness and runners who need a secure, ear-canal-free fit.

items.title: Hisense takes on JBL and Ultimate Ears with its first outdoor Bluetooth speaker lineup
items.summary: Hisense launched three outdoor portable Bluetooth speakers - FlexBoom, WeBoom and VoyageBoom - first shown at CES 2026 and now available in the US, marking the TV giant's push into the portable audio market against established players JBL and Ultimate Ears.

items.title: Soundboks just launched its smallest and lightest party speaker yet
items.summary: Soundboks launched the Rider, its most compact and lightest speaker to date at just 6.3kg, capable of outputting up to 118dB. The IP66-rated portable party speaker extends the brand's loud-outdoor lineup into a more transportable form factor.

items.title: Yamaha's new soundbar offers big bass in a tiny package
items.summary: Yamaha launched the B200A, its most compact Dolby Atmos soundbar yet at just 23.5 inches wide, featuring a built-in subwoofer and Bass Extension technology for deeper low-end from a small footprint aimed at apartments and smaller living rooms.

items.title: Voicemod's new pocket-friendly device brings real-time voice changing to your phone
items.summary: Voicemod announced a new mobile device that extends its real-time voice-changing Key dongle to phones, letting users apply sound effects and a soundboard on the go. The hardware builds on the console-focused Voicemod Key launched in late 2024 and broadens the company's reach into mobile creators.

items.title: Ikea supersized its cheap Bluetooth speaker and added an optical input
items.summary: Ikea's new Badkruka wireless Bluetooth speaker is now available in the US for 59.99 dollars, a much larger follow-up to its tiny 10-dollar Kallsup speaker from CES 2026. At nearly seven inches tall, it adds an optical input for TV connection while keeping the brand's budget-friendly positioning.

items.title: Anker announces its first over-the-counter hearing aids
items.summary: Anker debuted its first over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids at IFA 2026, entering a market where two major US OTC makers recently wound down operations. The launch positions the audio accessory giant to capture demand from cost-conscious consumers with mild-to-moderate hearing loss.

items.title: JBL takes on Sonos with new multi-room Cove speakers
items.summary: JBL introduced the Cove series of connected speakers that can run independently, as a stereo pair, or linked into a multi-room sound system. The lineup marks the portable and party-speaker specialist's formal move into whole-home, app-controlled audio to challenge Sonos.
